description: Dimension count excluding the 'degenerating 4-form' route to SU(3): Spin(7) is not the stabilizer of a generic 4-form on R^8 (codim 27), and no 4-form on R^8 can be generic at all since dim GL(8) = 64 < dim Lambda^4 = 70. G_2 from a 3-form on R^7 is by contrast an open orbit. Bean qou-8p1f.

data.verdict: the 'perhaps the 4-form degenerates' route to SU(3) fails by genericity: the Cayley/Spin(7) locus is codimension 27 and no 4-form on R^8 has an open orbit, so a tetraplectic or arbitrary 4-form does not degenerate into a Spin(7) structure -- it would have to be imposed, which is a LARGER octonionic import than the status quo since Spin(7) contains G_2
data.constructive_reading: the generic-form route runs through 3-forms in dimension 7, not 4-forms in dimension 8; the lower link G_2 -> SU(3) via S^6 = G_2/SU(3) is untouched and is already eightfold open-problem item 3, which is where form-stabilizer effort belongs
data.scope: scope-(b) for the specific claim 'a generic/tetraplectic 4-form on an 8-manifold degenerates to Spin(7)', excluded by a dimension count
not_excluded: imposing a Cayley form by hand (consistent; not a derivation)
tetraplectic geometry generally -- see qou-8p1g for the separate m = 1 vacuity observation
routes not going through generic-form stabilizers (Bruhat, multi-fibre groupoid)
